lines.trans: I am the head chef of this restaurant.
Does everything suit you?
Thank you, everything is very delicious.
Turn around carefully.
Are you not acquainted with the woman by the kitchen?
No, I am seeing her for the first time.
Stay far away from her.
Under no circumstances talk to her.
What, is she some kind of swindler?
We are not sure, we suspect so.
I talked to her, she does not want to meet.
Very sad, I will go then.

words.gloss: it is a pity, too bad

lines.trans: Lena, wait for me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'head chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am the head chef of this restaurant.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Витя, в ресторане всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Vitya, is everything alright in the restaurant?
I am the head chef of this restaurant.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you two chatting here?

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Вы с Викой расстались, и она сразу кого-то нашла?
examples.trans: You and Vika broke up, and she immediately found someone?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.
Alright, it is settled, we are going.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'страивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'suits / satisfies', paired with 'устроить'.

examples.trans: Does everything suit you?

examples.text: Мне нужно как-то устраивать новую жизнь.
examples.trans: I need to arrange a new life somehow.
I did not stage anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Nastya!
Thank you, everything is very delicious.
Thank you for your vigilance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
Do you want to ruin our relationship?

examples.text: Если ты не хочешь, я не буду тебя заставлять.
examples.trans: If you do not want to, I will not force you.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Thank you, everything is very delicious.
It's delicious!
Mum is a good cook.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Turn around carefully.
Easy, Vanya, be careful!
Drive the car carefully.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вернуться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turn around'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и повернуться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and turn around on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют повернуться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to turn around.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('acquainted').

examples.text: Познакомь, а то мне придётся Катю просить.
examples.trans: Introduce us, or else I will have to ask Katya.

examples.text: Вы не знакомы с женщиной у кухни?
examples.trans: Are you not acquainted with the woman by the kitchen?
I talked to her, she does not want to meet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы не знакомы с женщиной у кухни?
examples.trans: Are you not acquainted with the woman by the kitchen?
She is a wise woman.
Who is that woman?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
The rookie has returned!
We need to talk!

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Вы не знакомы с женщиной у кухни?
examples.trans: Are you not acquainted with the woman by the kitchen?
We're sitting in the kitchen.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, black and white.
No, I am seeing her for the first time.

examples.text: Мне очень нужно знать, мой это ребёнок или нет.
examples.trans: I really need to know whether this child is mine or not.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She is a good one you have.
Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
Maybe she was joking?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for the first time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, I am seeing her for the first time.

examples.text: Я впервые в жизни вижу такое.
examples.trans: I see such a thing for the first time in my life.

examples.text: Но с ним я впервые в жизни счастлива.
examples.trans: But with him I am happy for the first time in my life.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Я её после этого не видел.
examples.trans: I did not see her after that.
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stick (with)'.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?
I need to stay further away from her.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
Work does not wait, it is time to run.
Do you want to ruin our relationship?

meanings.en: far, far away, a long way
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We've already gone so far.
The shop is far from the house.

examples.text: Насколько далеко зашло всё это следствие?
examples.trans: How far has this whole investigation gone?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not even, nor', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
You have such a wonderful boss.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
Vika, wait!
We need to talk!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'any / which', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.
She left him alone with a daughter.
With her grandmother and grandfather.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What happened?

examples.text: Ни в коем случае не общайтесь с ней.
examples.trans: Under no circumstances talk to her.
Alright, what happened?

meanings.en: to communicate, to socialise, to have contact
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'talk / associate'.

examples.trans: I am not allowed to talk with you.
We talk often.

examples.text: Мне с вами вообще общаться нельзя. Всего доброго.
examples.trans: I'm not allowed to talk to you at all. Good day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!
We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'con artist / swindler' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What, is she some kind of swindler?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть мошенница.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always con artist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It turns out we are friends in misfortune.
Katya and I broke up.
We are exchanging curious facts, after all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'веренный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('confident, sure').

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный.
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident.
He answered in a calm, confident voice.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный. Что конкретно?
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident. What specifically?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'озревать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'suspect'.

examples.trans: We are not sure, we suspect so.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подозревать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and suspect on time.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
Go to our place, we will talk tonight.
I need to talk with the doctor.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wants', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.
Kostya wanted to cover for me.
I want coffee.

meanings.en: to get acquainted, to meet (someone new)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet / get acquainted', paired with 'познакомиться'.

examples.trans: I talked to her, she does not want to meet.
Well then, let's get acquainted.
Meet Vika.

жаль.gloss: it is a pity, too bad

meanings.en: it is a pity, too bad
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it is a pity, too bad', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Так сбежал, что ты до него не доберёшься.
examples.trans: He ran so far that you will not reach him.
Please, hear me out.
I held back.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
That simply cannot be!
Aha, then everything is clear.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: The money will go to charity.

examples.text: Мне с работы позвонили, я пойду.
examples.trans: They called me from work, I will go.
Very sad, I will go then.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
